# V2: an original rover model, generated by script, 2026-11-15

**Status: mesh generator done and checked in Blender. Not yet imported into Unreal.** The images below are
**Blender renders**, not game screenshots. The pawn change, the Unreal import, and same-condition
before-and-after shots with GPU time wait for the Mac, as the [visual roadmap](../../visual-roadmap.md) requires.

## What was made

[`scripts/blender/build_rover.py`](../../../scripts/blender/build_rover.py) builds four visual meshes from primitives.
It uses no third-party geometry or textures. Sizes come from the pawn's constants in
`unreal/Source/Roverloom/Rover/RoverDrive.h`, which follow `rovers/designs/pathfinder_6w.json`.

| Mesh | Origin and axes | Triangles | Role in the pawn |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SM_RoverBody` | Body center; +X forward, +Y left, +Z up | 4,068 | Replaces the greybox body parts: chassis, 6 m² solar deck, mast and camera head at 2.0 m, rocker-bogie arms, hazard cameras, stowed sample arm, antenna |
| `SM_RoverWheel` | Axle center; axle along Y | 2,152 | Replaces each wheel cylinder and its spin bar. Radius 0.25 m including grousers, width 0.20 m |
| `SM_RoverStrut` | Center; 1 m tall | 12 | Replaces each leg. The pawn keeps scaling Z by the wheel's drop |
| `SM_RoverAxle` | Wheel center; reaches 0.18 m along -Y | 72 | New: joins the hub to the strut. Mirrored in Y on the other side. Does not spin |

The whole rover is about 17,500 triangles at rest. Six material slots (`M_RoverBody`, `M_RoverFoil`,
`M_RoverAluminum`, `M_RoverDark`, `M_RoverSolar`, `M_RoverGlass`) carry flat preview colors only. Unreal materials are
made in Unreal, from original or CC0 sources.

**One change from the greybox:** the rocker-bogie arms and struts move 0.16 m inboard of the wheels' center planes, to
y = ±0.877 m. In the greybox they ran through the wheels. This is visual only. Wheel mounts, contact, and the rig are
unchanged.

## Checks, from `report.json`

Run with the `bpy` module 5.0.1 (Blender 5.0.1) on Linux, in a temporary cloud container.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Wheel outer radius equals the physics radius, 0.25 m, within 2 mm | 0.250 m, passed |
| Wheel half width | 0.100 m, passed |
| Wheel bottom on flat ground at rest (body center 0.70 m up, drop 0.25 m) | Passed |
| No body vertex inside any wheel's swept volume at rest | 0 vertices, passed |
| Struts clear of the wheels' inner faces | 0.035 m, passed |
| Axle reaches the strut | Passed |
| Body clearance above flat ground | 0.47 m |
| Mast top above flat ground | 2.11 m (camera head at 2.0 m, as in the pawn) |

Not checked here: clearance while a wheel drops to full travel, or with the body tilted. Both are visual
overlaps only. Check them in Unreal on the step and ramp lanes.

## Renders

Cycles on CPU, 48 samples, 1280 × 720, JPEG quality 88. One sun, a flat ground in V1b's regolith color, and a uniform
sky color. These are not the game's lighting.

Four views: front three-quarter, side, rear from above, and the game's chase-camera distance (9 m, 70°).
**They are not in Git:** this cloud session could not upload Git LFS objects. Regenerate them with `--render` as
below. They go to `unreal/Saved/RoverModel/preview_*.jpg`, about 30–60 KB each. Commit them from the Mac if wanted.

## Reproduce

```shell
blender -b -P scripts/blender/build_rover.py -- --out unreal/Saved/RoverModel --render
```

Or with the `bpy` module from PyPI, in its own virtual environment, using Python 3.11:

```shell
python -I scripts/blender/build_rover.py --out unreal/Saved/RoverModel --render
```

Outputs go to `unreal/Saved/`, which Git ignores. The script exits with status 1 if any check fails.

## Unreal integration: written, not yet built

Written in a cloud session without Unreal. **Not compiled, imported, or run.** The Mac run decides whether it works.

- [`scripts/unreal/import_rover_meshes.py`](../../../scripts/unreal/import_rover_meshes.py): Editor Python. It
  imports the four FBX files into `/Game/Rover/` without collision, and logs each mesh's bounds.
- `ARoverPawn::ApplyModelV2` (`unreal/Source/Roverloom/Rover/RoverPawn.cpp`): at `BeginPlay`, it loads the four meshes
  if they exist. Otherwise it logs `Rover model: greybox` and changes nothing.
  - With the meshes, it hides the greybox parts and the rig's body box. Hiding them changes rendering only, not
    collision or physics.
  - It shows the body mesh, gives each wheel the new mesh, which spins about its own Y axis, moves the struts inboard
    to y = ±87.7 cm, and adds an axle per wheel.
  - It reads which way the imported axle points, and mirrors it per side. It logs the body and wheel bounds, and warns
    if they differ from the generator's (body X −175.0 to +113.5 cm, wheel radius 25 cm).
- `-RoverModel=greybox` keeps the old look, for before-and-after shots under the same conditions.
- No physics, command, mission-link, or HUD code changed.

## Next, on the Mac

1. Build the meshes, then import them:

   ```shell
   blender -b -P scripts/blender/build_rover.py -- --out unreal/Saved/RoverModel
   ```

   ```shell
   "$UE_ROOT/Engine/Binaries/Mac/UnrealEditor.app/Contents/MacOS/UnrealEditor" "$PWD/unreal/Roverloom.uproject" -run=pythonscript -script="$PWD/scripts/unreal/import_rover_meshes.py $PWD/unreal/Saved/RoverModel"
   ```

   If UE 5.8 imports FBX through Interchange and ignores these options, import the files by hand with collision off,
   and record what was done.
2. Build the C++ project, and run the automation tests, as in [unreal/README.md](../../../unreal/README.md).
3. Run the game. Check the `Rover model: V2` log line, and look at all four cameras. The lenses should face forward,
   the wheels should spin the right way, and the struts and axles should meet.
4. Run the drive scripts `f1-flat`, `f1-step`, and `f1-ramp15` with and without `-RoverModel=greybox`. The phase logs
   must match within run-to-run spread, because only rendering changed.
5. Take same-condition shots against [V1b](../v1b-terrain/README.md), and record GPU time. The limit is +0.5 ms.
6. Make materials in Unreal from original or CC0 sources. The FBX import brings only flat colors.
7. Lock and commit the `.uasset` files through LFS, then update this page and the README's screenshot.

## Concept renders with vork

[ADR 0015](../../decisions/0015-vork-for-concept-renders.md) adopts vork for concept renders. The generator
[`scripts/vork/rover_concept.py`](../../../scripts/vork/rover_concept.py) writes three scenes (`hero`, `side`,
`sunset`) from this model's `rover_preview.glb`. The GLB now holds only the assembled rover: the unplaced
wheel, strut, and axle originals are removed before export.

| Check, in a Linux cloud container without a GPU, vork 0.5.1 | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `vork check` on `hero`, `side`, `sunset` | `Scene checked successfully`, all three |
| `vork check --shaders` on `hero`, which also compiles portable shaders, including the dust program, on the CPU | `Scene checked successfully`, in 3 min 52 s |

No image has been rendered: that needs the Mac. See the [guide](../../vork-concept-renders.md).
